goal: Bind red retention to judged content and preserve interrupted executions while classifying external interpreter crashes correctly
asset: Attestation wrapper, fault policy and sequential reference reruns
scope: Content and commit identities on every local citation
No-nonce and unfinished execution retention after launch
Actual judged-tree dirt, failure hook coverage, pseudo-frame and xdist crash parsing
Self-contained exact Git snapshots for reference legs
outOfScope: Excusing assertion failures, timeouts, repository crashes or unknown unfinished executions
Native Windows live crash reproduction in this Linux executor

record.question: What identity and evidence keep a failed gate from being erased by a later green?

options.strongest_objection: Legacy rows need conservative handling and old local claims need a judged sha
An empty commit, a missing nonce or a killed runner erases red scope

record.rationale: Bind claims to exact judged commits, group retained failures by content plus dirt, and block unknown incomplete executions.
evidence: Issue177 reproduces red laundering by empty commits, missing nonce and killed runners
The gate runner already retains process identity and Git commit provenance

costs.cost: One Git tree-object observation and bounded retained-record scan
Unsettled red executions disappear from scope

requirements.statement: Every local claim names its exact judged commit, and reds for the same content/dirt survive empty commits, missing nonce and unfinished/error runner records.
requirements.counterexample: A later green at another commit or after killing the runner erases a retained red

requirements.statement: Failure hooks retain runtime exit errors, clean linked gates ignore unrelated root edits, external pseudo-frame/xdist crashes classify, and references run exact committed bytes with Git metadata.
requirements.counterexample: A missing .git or truncated xdist summary blocks a valid reference pair

checks.scope: Actual gates, linked worktree and Git clone; deterministic retained records and stack fixtures
assumptions: Local execution records remain an honest-executor boundary
No Linux fixture establishes native Windows process-exit translation

challenges.claim: Can unknown or killed executions be treated as successful cancellation?
challenges.resolution: No. Unknown records remain blockers; only authenticated cancellation and fresh covering CI evidence can yield.
